    Generate a General SE/Matérn Covariance Function

    cov_generator.Rd

    Creates a covariance function that computes either the Squared Exponential (SE) kernel (when nu = Inf) or the Matérn kernel (for finite nu) between two sets of input points in \(d\)-dimensional space.

    cov_generator(length_scale = 1, signal_var = 1, nu = Inf)

    Arguments

    length_scale

    A positive numeric scalar or vector. If scalar, the same length-scale is used for all dimensions. If a vector, its length must equal the number of columns of the input data.

    signal_var

    Positive numeric scalar specifying the signal variance (\(\sigma^2\)).

    nu

    Positive numeric specifying the smoothness parameter for the Matérn kernel. Use Inf to select the Squared Exponential kernel.

    Value

    A function cov_fun(x, x_prime) which accepts:

    • x: numeric matrix or vector (observations in rows).

    • x_prime: numeric matrix or vector (observations in rows).

    and returns the covariance matrix between x and x_prime.

    Details

    The returned function first rescales each dimension by length_scale, then computes the pairwise squared Euclidean distances. - If nu = Inf, it returns the SE kernel: $$K_{ij} = \sigma^2 \exp\bigl(-\tfrac{1}{2} \|x_i - x'_j\|^2\bigr).$$ - Otherwise, it constructs the Matérn kernel with smoothness nu: $$K_{ij} = \sigma^2 \frac{2^{1-\nu}}{\Gamma(\nu)} \bigl(\sqrt{2\nu}\,r_{ij}\bigr)^\nu K_\nu\bigl(\sqrt{2\nu}\,r_{ij}\bigr),$$ where \(r_{ij} = \|x_i - x'_j\|\). Internally, for half-integer nu this is computed via an exact polynomial–exponential form.

    Examples

    # 1D SE kernel
se_cov <- cov_generator(length_scale = 0.5, signal_var = 2, nu = Inf)
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 5)
se_cov(x, x)
#>           [,1]      [,2]     [,3]      [,4]      [,5]
#> [1,] 2.0000000 1.7649938 1.213061 0.6493049 0.2706706
#> [2,] 1.7649938 2.0000000 1.764994 1.2130613 0.6493049
#> [3,] 1.2130613 1.7649938 2.000000 1.7649938 1.2130613
#> [4,] 0.6493049 1.2130613 1.764994 2.0000000 1.7649938
#> [5,] 0.2706706 0.6493049 1.213061 1.7649938 2.0000000

# 2D Matérn kernel with nu = 1.5
matern_cov <- cov_generator(length_scale = c(1, 2), signal_var = 1, nu = 1.5)
X <- matrix(runif(10), ncol = 2)
matern_cov(X, X)
#>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]      [,5]
#> [1,] 1.0000000 0.9196272 0.8207043 0.9203015 0.8264377
#> [2,] 0.9196272 1.0000000 0.8749076 0.8823816 0.9482185
#> [3,] 0.8207043 0.8749076 1.0000000 0.9383814 0.9379758
#> [4,] 0.9203015 0.8823816 0.9383814 1.0000000 0.8698880
#> [5,] 0.8264377 0.9482185 0.9379758 0.8698880 1.0000000
